uncited: The standard 3D Gaussian Splatting primitive is defined by a center $\mu_i$, a covariance matrix $\Sigma_i$ (parameterized by rotation $R_i$ and scaling $S_i$), opacity $\alpha_i$, and color $c_i$ [Parent].
**Orientation:** Adding a normal vector $n_i$ [9621-oriented-gaussian-splatting.md] or skewness parameter $k_i$ [10045-3d-skew-normal-splatting.md] to define directional attenuation or asymmetry.
**Constraint:** Constraining centers $\mu_i$ to lie on a mesh surface using barycentric coordinates [15283-barycentric-splat-parameterization.md].
Standard 3D Gaussian Splatting [Parent] uses isotropic or anisotropic Gaussians for view synthesis but lacks explicit geometric primitives for surface reconstruction.

Oriented Gaussian Splatting introduces normals for surface wrapping [9621-oriented-gaussian-splatting.md]. 3D Skew-Normal Splatting uses skew-normal distributions for asymmetry [10045-3d-skew-normal-splatting.md].
Barycentric Splat Parameterization binds Gaussians to meshes using barycentric coordinates [15283-barycentric-splat-parameterization.md].
Anisotropic covariance allows 3D Gaussians to scale along x, y, and z axes and rotate in 3D space to better fit scene geometry [11879-anisotropic-covariance.md].
